title: How do we mark parallel and perpendicular lines in five shapes?
description: Five shapes are drawn on a dot grid. The board marks parallel sides with one, two or three arrows and right angles with a square, shape by shape, and then says how to spot each kind of line.
teaching_notes: One idea: sides that repeat the same steps are parallel, and a flat side meeting an upright side makes a right angle. Check every arrow mark sits on exactly two sides.

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q2
video_script.why: The child knows the arrow marks and the square mark and now uses them on five shapes.
video_script.substitution: Put arrow marks on the parallel sides and a square at each right angle, the same way as the example in the book, then say how each kind of line was spotted.
video_script.anchor: Five shapes drawn on a dot grid, numbered one to five.
video_script.payoff_line: Shape one has two pairs of parallel sides and one right angle.

final_answer.value: Shape 1: two pairs parallel and one right angle; shape 2: two pairs; shape 3: three pairs and two right angles; shape 4: one right angle; shape 5: two pairs and three right angles. (a) Flat and upright lines meet at 90°. (b) Same steps, same gap
final_answer.spoken: shape one has two pairs of parallel sides and one right angle

hold_back: Shape 1: two pairs parallel and one right angle; shape 2: two pairs; shape 3: three pairs and two right angles; shape 4: one right angle; shape 5: two pairs and three right angles. (a) Flat and upright lines meet at 90°. (b) Same steps, same gap
maths_rules: shape 1: (0,0) to (2,2) and (2,4) to (3,5) lean the same way, so parallel with one arrow; the upright sides (2,2) to (2,4) and (0,5) to (0,0) are parallel with two arrows; one right angle at (0,5)
shape 2: the flat sides (6,1) to (10,1) and (8,3) to (4,3) are parallel with one arrow; (10,1) to (8,3) and (4,3) to (6,1) both go 2 across and 2 down, so parallel with two arrows; no right angle
shape 3: three pairs of parallel sides, one, two and three arrows; right angles at (7,8) and (5,6)
shape 4: one right angle at (0,7), no parallel sides
shape 5: flat sides parallel with one arrow, upright sides parallel with two arrows; right angles at (5,9), (5,11) and (11,11)
perpendicular lines on the grid: a flat line and an upright line meet at a right angle; parallel lines repeat the same steps, so the gap stays the same
video_script.design: The five shapes stay on the stage. Arrow marks and squares are added one shape at a time, and the shape being checked is picked out.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, shape one. Two sides lean the same way, so they get one arrow each.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The two upright sides are parallel, so they get two arrows each.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>An upright side meets the flat bottom, so we draw a square there. That is one right angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: shape 2 has two pairs of parallel sides and no right angle

marks.m1: the two flat sides of shape 2 light up and get one arrow each
marks.m2: the two slanting sides of shape 2 light up and get two arrows each
marks.m3: the corners of shape 2 are checked and no square is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, shape two. The two flat sides are parallel, so they get one arrow each.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The two slanting sides both go two across and two down, so they get two arrows each.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>No flat side meets an upright side, so there is no right angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: shape 3 has three pairs of parallel sides, with one, two and three arrows, and two right angles

marks.m1: the leaning pair of shape 3 gets one arrow each
marks.m2: the upright pair gets two arrows each and the flat pair gets three arrows each
marks.m3: squares are drawn at the two corners where a flat side meets an upright side

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, shape three. It has three pairs of parallel sides. The leaning pair gets one arrow each.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The upright pair gets two arrows each, and the flat pair gets three arrows each.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two corners join a flat side to an upright side. Each gets a square, so there are two right angles.

marks.m2: the flat pair of shape 5 gets one arrow each and the upright pair gets two arrows each
marks.m3: squares are drawn at the three corners of shape 5 where a flat side meets an upright side

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, shape four. It has one right angle and no parallel sides.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Shape five has a flat pair with one arrow each, and an upright pair with two arrows each.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three corners join a flat side to an upright side. Each gets a square.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step five, check the marks. Every arrow mark sits on exactly two sides.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Shape 1: two pairs parallel and one right angle; shape 2: two pairs; shape 3: three pairs and two right angles; shape 4: one right angle; shape 5: two pairs and three right angles. (a) Flat and upright lines meet at 90°. (b) Same steps, same gap

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Shape one has two pairs of parallel sides and one right angle.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Shape two has two pairs. Shape three has three pairs and two right angles.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Shape four has one right angle. Shape five has two pairs and three right angles.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>We spot perpendicular lines as a flat line meeting an upright line. We spot parallel lines by the same steps and the same gap.
